q: It took a month to get insurance sorted and then TWO months to find a practice that would accept me with two practices taking 3 weeks each to deliberate before they told me they wouldn't accept me.
cx: Moved to Florida at 16 weeks in her second pregnancy.

q: By the time my appointment came around, it had been 3 months since I'd been seen by a doctor.
cx: The gap in care after moving.

q: they told me that the only females they have at the practice are NPs and it will be a male delivering me no matter what. Direct opposite of what I've been told up to that point.
cx: After asking for a female OB who could deliver her.

q: I specifically requested an appointment with an OB who could be delivering me because my first pregnancy ended in an emergency c section after a 24 hour labor and I wanted to see what they thought my options are
each of them always sat in the room with me asking me questions about myself and my pregnancy and asking if I had any questions. None of them ever left the room until they were sure I was comfortable
cx: Her small-town practice in another state during her first pregnancy.

q: yes that's annoying, but we have to wait months AND we pay so much money on top of that. No system is perfect, but half the reason we had to move to Florida for a few years is because of medical debt.
cx: Comparing US waits and costs with Canada's.

q: I’m just really grateful for my MIL who is already setting up a room dedicated for my child in her house and talking about making arrangements to help me watch the child. My mom even told me she’s in her prime and there not much she can do.
cx: Seven weeks; her own mother keeps her distance, her future mother-in-law steps in.

q: I see my mom’s perspective but can’t help but want to scream you’re the mom not me. Just step up and get involved and stop waiting on me!
cx: What she wants from her mother.

q: Even my MIL checks in on me more often than my mom does.
cx: Early pregnancy, comparing the two mothers.

q: My company is not paying for my leave but I have to wonder if my progressive write ups within close proximity is just them trying to find write ups to push me out the door. I’m worried I’ll be fired before going into labor thus not qualifying for paid leave.
cx: 28 weeks, restaurant assistant manager, a second write-up coming.

q: I’m living paycheck to paycheck so no income is just not doable. Do I wait this out and work myself harder until I give birth? Or do I take action now and get myself out of this early?
cx: Weighing a job change at 28 weeks.

q: I'm just trying to survive until then, I have the nesting *need* but I have no energy or ability to move.
the OB said I kinda just have to deal with it until he comes naturally or my induction date.
cx: Her OB's answer to severe pain at 37 weeks.

q: I'm very early in my pregnancy and the anxiety over the upcoming bloodwork is already completely consuming me.
Has anyone else who faints immediately managed to get through this? What did you say to the phlebotomist to make it go better?
cx: What she asks before her first bloods.
